texts.orig: Q: I’m overwhelmed with work and wondering if you have any productivity tips that help you stay above water?
texts.text: Q: I’m overwhelmed with work and wondering if you have any productivity tips that help you stay above water?

texts.label: text
texts.orig: There are a lot of big ideas out there for how to use your time most effectively, but sometimes you just need a few really good tricks. Over the years, I’ve read dozens of productivity books and tried a bunch of stuff. Most of the ideas work for a few weeks and then fade. But below are 10 techniques that have stuck with me. I use them daily, and they consistently help me get more stuff done. Pick a few to try and see how it goes for you.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: . The core idea is that any work of real value comes from people doing “deep work”—focused, uninterrupted, and cognitively demanding work that stretches their brain. Unfortunately, most of our time is spent on “shallow work”—not cognitively demanding, logistical-style tasks, often performed while distracted. And that’s totally OK, as long as you get enough deep work time in.
texts.text: . The core idea is that any work of real value comes from people doing “deep work”—focused, uninterrupted, and cognitively demanding work that stretches their brain. Unfortunately, most of our time is spent on “shallow work”—not cognitively demanding, logistical-style tasks, often performed while distracted. And that’s totally OK, as long as you get enough deep work time in.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: It takes time to get into a deep work state (30 to 60 minutes) and, more importantly, you need to avoid distractions to stay in this mode. What worked really well for me while I was working full-time was creating two to three recurring blocks each week that were dedicated to deep work time. Those were basically the only time I got “real” work done, and I treasured them.

texts.orig: 10. Say no more often, even when it’s hard
texts.text: 10. Say no more often, even when it’s hard

texts.label: text
texts.orig: I can’t write a productivity guide for product managers without also encouraging you to say no more often. It’s a rule.
texts.text: I can’t write a productivity guide for product managers without also encouraging you to say no more often. It’s a rule.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Most of our burnout and overwhelm comes not from a lack of productivity tools and tricks, but from taking on too much work. The more you can do up front to make your workload less full, the better everything gets downstream.
texts.text: Most of our burnout and overwhelm comes not from a lack of productivity tools and tricks, but from taking on too much work. The more you can do up front to make your workload less full, the better everything gets downstream.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: To help you say no more often, I pulled some tactical advice from previous pieces I’ve written:
texts.text: To help you say no more often, I pulled some tactical advice from previous pieces I’ve written:

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Filter asks through your priorities:
texts.text: Filter asks through your priorities:

texts.label: text
texts.orig: What are the two or three things you must do well to be successful in your work and life?
